🇲🇽✊ <u>42.8 Million People in Mexico Now Receive Welfare Programs</u>

Welfare Secretary Leticia Ramírez Amaya told the Chamber of Deputies that 42.8 million people now receive the Programas para el Bienestar. By the end of 2026, more than one trillion pesos will have gone to pensions, scholarships and social support. Almost 14 million older adults get the universal pension from age 65, at about 527 billion pesos a year. Another 2.8 million women aged 60 to 64 receive the Women's Pension, and 1.8 million people with disabilities receive theirs. She said more than 13.4 million people left poverty in six years.

🇲🇽🏙️ <u>Four State Congresses Form One Parliament for 22 Million People</u>

Lawmakers from Mexico City, the State of Mexico, Hidalgo and Morelos signed the founding protocol of the Metropolitan Parliament of the Valley of Mexico. It is a permanent body for passing joint laws on water, transport, security and public services in a region of more than 22 million people. It covers 84 municipalities and boroughs: 16 in Mexico City, 59 in the State of Mexico, 8 in Hidalgo and 1 in Morelos. The four congresses also signed a Metropolitan Legislative Pact to protect family incomes in the 2027 budget year.

🇲🇽🏗️ <u>Mexico's Construction Output Jumps 10.6% in a Year</u>

The value of output from Mexico's construction companies rose 10.6% in August compared with August 2025, according to INEGI's National Survey of Construction Companies. From January to August it is up 4.19%. Month to month it held flat after a 2.2% drop in July. The biggest annual gains were in the south and center: Tabasco +145.2%, Hidalgo +104%, Oaxaca +89.1%.

The Governor of Chihuahua is speaking with the President of the Republic. So my obligation was to tell her: proceed." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 23, 2026 In an interview with Carlos Loret de Mola, Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos (PAN) said she and Sheinbaum shouted at each other at a meeting in the Ciudad Juárez airport. Sheinbaum gave her own account. Campos reproached her over the treason accusation. Then Campos said it was her former state prosecutor who let the agents in, and that they had found corruption by him, including casinos. Sheinbaum told her to proceed through the state prosecutor's office and the Attorney General's Office. Chihuahua's prosecutors then charged him first.

🇲🇽🎨 "The right does not recognize democracy as government of the people. The right seeks for everyone to think the same." "Mexico is a very special country. These right-wing ideas are hardly accepted by the people, because it is conscious of its history and has memory." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 23, 2026 A reporter asked about the Festival de Escribidores, an event of the Mario Vargas Llosa Chair hosted by Ricardo Salinas Pliego's Escuela de la Libertad. Sheinbaum said the guests are arriving in a free, democratic country, or they couldn't come. Some in the cultural world are angry because they lost their closeness to government and its money. She recalled Madrid's Isabel Díaz Ayuso coming to promote Hernán Cortés: "it did not go very well." She cited independence, the Reform and the Revolution: "the epic of the Mexican people," as Diego Rivera put it.

text: 🇲🇽✊ "The biggest corruption in the past was the big distributors. They outsourced the whole system, and they charged eight times what the system cost." "President López Obrador started it, and we are going to complete it: a distribution service that is mainly public, developed by young Mexican scientists. That way, capacities of the Mexican State are built that were lost during the whole neoliberal period." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 23, 2026 A reporter asked about supplies being stolen and resold. Sheinbaum said such cases exist and must be reported, but they can't be generalized: most health workers save lives every day. She called the attacks a paid campaign. Under the old model, even hospital pharmacies were run by private firms, on 10- to 15-year contracts, with kickbacks to officials.

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "Zero privileges. Let us never forget where we come from. We come from a movement that fought against the privileges of a few. It cannot be that you get to where you are and your objective is privilege." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 23, 2026 A reporter asked about senators who requested access to the protocol lounge at Mexico City's international airport, criticized online as VIP treatment. "We would not lend them. Of course not." Later in the same conference, Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco confirmed the request had been made, and that the Foreign Ministry said no. Her message to legislators: "Don't forget where you come from."
